sentences.text: Researchers conducted a retrospective study involving 111 patients with early-stage behavioral variant frontotemporal dementia, a mean age of 63.03 years, to evaluate personality traits and daily living abilities using data from knowledgeable informants.

While patients exhibited significant shifts in personality, including reduced conscientiousness and increased neuroticism, no association was found between pre-disease personality and current functional independence, though higher current conscientiousness was linked to better performance in daily tasks.

The authors concluded that the study's cross-sectional design and reliance on recalled information limit these findings, stating that future longitudinal studies with direct performance tests are required to confirm the results.
